Issuance: Personal Data Protection Order (PDPO)
Data ownership and accountability rules:
-An organisation is responsible for personal data in its possession or under its control.

- An organisation shall appoint Data Protection Officer (“DPO”) to oversee compliances with PDPO. An organisation must make available to the public the business contact information of at least one of the individuals designated under the above requirements.

- An organisation to implement PDP policies and communicate them to all staff.
Data security and confidentiality standa: Organisations shall reasonably secure and protect all personal data in their possession or under their control from unauthorised access and processing; and the loss of any storage device containing the personal data.
Consent management standards:
Obtaining individual's consent prior to processing of personal data, unless authorised by law or an exception under the new legislation applies. Consent is validly obtained and expressly given or deemed to have been given.

*Standards for valid consent
- provided with the information required
- provided his consent for that purpose
- given in written or other form so as to be accessible for subsequent reference.  (for telephone number)

*Standards for deemed consent
- voluntarily provides the personal data to the organisation for that purpose
-reasonable that the individual would voluntarily provide the data.

*Standards for deemed consent by notification
- the individual does not notify the organisation, before the expiry of the period mentioned in subsection (3)(b}(iii), that the individual does not consent to the proposed collection, use or disclosure of the personal data by the organisation.
Data retention and archiving requirement: Organisations to stop retaining personal data information, as soon as it is assume that the personal data no longer serves the purpose for which it was collected, or any other legal or business purpose.​
Data sharing and interoperability standa: Individuals must be notified of the purposes for which their data will be collected, used, or disclosed.
Cross-border data transfer conditions: Organisations shall not transfer personal data to a country or territory outside Brunei Darussalam unless there is a similar or better data protection law available. An alternative is to have contracts with specific instruction on data protection across borders.
Data quality and integrity standards:
An organisation shall make a reasonable  effort that personal data collected by or on behalf  of the organisation is accurate and complete if the
personal data -
(a)is likely to be used by the organisation to make a decision that affects the individual to whom the personal data relates; or
(b)is likely to be disclosed by the organisation to another organisation.
Incident/breach notification timelines:
Organisation shall conduct, in a reasonable and expeditious manner, an assessment of whether a data breach is a notifiable data breach.

*Notifiable data breaches
-results in, or is likely to result in, significant harm to an affected individual (if the data breach is in relation to any prescribed personal data or class of personal data relating to the individual; or in other prescribed circumstances
-is likely to be of a significant scale (if the data breach affects not fewer than the prescribed number of
affected individuals; or in other prescribed circumstances)

-When an organization becomes aware of a data breach, it must conduct an assessment in a reasonable and expeditious to determine whether the breach is notifiable
- If a data processor suspects a data breach involving personal data it processes for another organization, it must promptly inform that organization, which is then responsible for assessing whether the breach is notifiable.
- Once the organization completes the assessment and concludes that the breach is notifiable, it must notify the Authority (AITI) as soon as practicable, and in any case no later than 3 calendar days after the assessment is completed.
-the organisation shall also notify each affected individual affected by a notifiable data breach
Third-party/outsourcing governance:
An organisation has the same obligation under this PDPO in respect of personal data processed on its behalf.

The organisation remains fully responsible for complying with the PDPO for personal data it outsources to a data processor. Legally, it is treated as if the organisation itself carried out the processing.

Issuance: Guidelines on Technology Risk Management(TRS/G-2/2022/1)
Information asset classification:
Classification is determined by FIs through the data asset management framework with the following metrics:
- risk
- security classification
- criticality

The regulation covers the following:
- personal data: whether true or not, about an individual who can be identified from that data; or from that data and other information to which the FI has or is likely to have access
-sensitive data
Data ownership and accountability rules:
-Data Ownership is established through data assset management framework by the financial institutions

-Accountability:
* Board & Senior Management- on important IT decision and operations in the FIs.
* Chief Information Officer - responsible to lead the IT management of the organization
* Chief Information Security Officer- responsible for management of information security and cybersecurity
* Business Units / System Owners — responsible for maintaining security controls, participate in risk reporting, and enforce segregation of duties
*End‑users and privileged users — users given access… should be held responsible and accountable for their own account
Data security and confidentiality standa:
- FIs should develop a comprehensive data loss prevention strategy to address data breach, theft, and leakage covering the following:
– Data at endpoints
– Data in motion (transmitted across networks)
– Data at rest (servers, databases, storage)
– Cloud data
Consent management standards:
- FIs must clearly indicate the purpose of data collection and obtain suitable consent from the customer.
- If there are changes to this policy affecting data protection, the FI must inform customers, and request renewed consent, as required
-For changes that require additional consent, the negative consent method must NOT be used.
The FI must follow up with customers to obtain affirmative consent.
- FIs must not obtain consent through force or unsolicited means.Instead, they may explain consequences of not providing consent. 
- FIs must provide clear disclaimers if their systems automatically collect data
- FIs must review the purpose of personal data usage and ensure it remains consistent with the consented purpose, especially after system or process changes.
Data retention and archiving requirement:
- FIs must retain logs for a period required by applicable legislation or regulation relating to log, record, or data retention.
- Logs must be retained and adequately protected to support potential investigations, including statutory document retention requirements.
-FIs must determine how long audit trail data will be maintained, aligned with the criticality of the systems, whether stored in-system or archived.
=
- FIs must archive logs using built‑in or third‑party archiving tools, and back them up to another storage medium.
-Central log collection servers are recommended to centralize logs for easier monitoring and retention.
-FIs must retain customer personal data in accordance with statutory or regulatory requirements for document retention, record keeping, and information protection.
-Where retention is mandated by law, these requirements must be communicated to customers.
Data sharing and interoperability standa:
-For Open APIs, data sharing must be limited to public information, read‑only, or one‑way processing
- Financial institutions should plan how to address compatibility and interoperability issues prior to integration, and ensure data and controls in the system are streamlined. this includes but not limited to the following:
- assess data structure and capacity of both systems
- assess potential changes to metadata where applicable
- optimize and test communication between the two systems or components
- ensure both systems are updated and security patches are installed
- review user access matrix for the new components and data, review security configuration of the new components
- prepare a testing plan that covers both systems, the components, and integration tool,
-prepare maintenance plans that covers the integrated systems of components of whole system
Cross-border data transfer conditions: Notification to  customers if storing personal data on a cloud platform or third party, including another country. Access to customer personal data should be restricted
Data quality and integrity standards:
-FIs should ensure their customer personal data are accurate, current and complete. The FIs should establish relevant process to request or allow customers to review and update their personal data.
-FIs should implement measures that ensure the confidentiality as well as integrity of audit trail data, such as the use of encryption, digital signatures and strong access controls.
-All logs should be protected from alteration or unauthorised removal. Access to the logs should be limited only to the designated administrator.
-FIs must classify data and assign ownership to support proper handling and integrity.
Encryption/cryptography prescriptions:
Encryption should cover the following:
- Sensitive data on servers, databases, endpoints, and storage media must be protected using strong encryption and access control.
- Communication or transfer of sensitive information must use:
*Encrypted channels (e.g., SSL, TLS),or (Encryption applied before transmission).
- Backup tapes/media  before off‑site transport.
- Digital services such as cards, e-wallets-biometric
- Audit trails
- Remote access
-Personal data sent online
-NFC

Cryptography
-Use well-established algorithms (e.g., RSA, AES) endorsed by international bodies.
-Define appropriate key length, ensure algorithms are rigorously tested, and ensure secure key generation, transmission, protection, and rotation.
-Keys must be sent through separate secure channels, and distribution media must be destroyed after use.
Incident/breach notification timelines:
Within 1 hour after suspected incident has been discovered
Within 2 hours from the discovery to confirm suspected incident is a near-miss or major IT incident
Third-party/outsourcing governance:
- If the Fls have to assign a third party to process customer personal data, the Fls should inform the customer on this arrangement and to limit access to personal data such as by using pseudonymisation or encryption.
-Fls has independent or direct access to relevant audit trails.
-The integrated third‑party system should not be able to access or extract data directly from the Fls’ main system, unless restricted on request and minimal basis
- FIs must evaluate third‑party data collection, storage, and protection.
-Ensure data for the API are separated from the main database.
-Data given from the API should be stored temporarily on a need basis only; cleared when session ends/idle.
-If the customer personal data has to be stored on a cloud platform or other third party, such arrangement including country where the customer's personal data is stored should be informed to the customer. Access to customer personal data must be restricted
Data Standards (e.g., ISO 20022): No explicit provision. However, the FI is required to observe new and existing laws and regulation in relation to personal data protection

Data ownership and accountability rules: No explicit provision

Customers must be given the choice to consent or refuse, be told the implications of refusal, and institutions must limit data collection to what is necessary and retain it only as needed or legally required.
Consent management standards: No explicit provision
Data retention and archiving requirement:
Where possible, banks and financial institutions shall limit the
amount of personal data collected to only what is necessary for its intended
purpose and may only be retained for the duration of its intended usage or
where legally required to do so.
Third-party/outsourcing governance: No explicit provision

Issuance: Prakas on the Management of Payment Service Providers
Data ownership and accountability rules:
Legal entities interested to provide payment services must submit an application to NBC with the following requirements:
- A description of the procedures for documenting, reviewing, monitoring and restricting the use of critical data
-A description of the principles and methods for collecting data related to transactions and fraud
Data security and confidentiality standa:
Legal entities interested to provide payment services must submit an application to NBC with the following requirements:
-Security policy, which includes a detailed assessment of the risks associated with payment services, including fraud, illegal use of personal data and sensitive data, along with a description of the security controls and measures to mitigate those risks.

Providers applying for a license on payment services must provide a description of the process in place to file, monitor, track and restrict access to sensitive payment data
Consent management standards: No explicit provision
Data retention and archiving requirement:
- payment service institution shall be entitled to store and process data after obtaining approval from the NBC
-Payment service institution shall set up contingency plan including data recovery system
Third-party/outsourcing governance:
-A Payment Services Provider shall guarantee that any third party acting on their behalf
comply with the legislation

Issuance: Personal Data Protection (PDP Law)
Information asset classification:
Personal data is classified into the following:
Special category Personal Data :Personal  Data which, if processed, may have a greater  impact on the Personal Data Subject,  including discriminatory treatment and  greater loss to a Personal Data Subject. This includes health data, biometric information,genetic data, criminal records,
General category Personal Data: Includes full name, gender, citizenship, religion, marriage status, cellular telephone number, IP address
Data ownership and accountability rules:
-A Personal Data Subject shall have the right to
acquire Information on the full identity, the legal
grounds, the purpose of the request and the use of
Personal Data, and the accountability of the party
requesting the Personal Data.
- Personal Data controllers is responsible for processing personal data
-Where Personal Data is processed by 2 (two)  or more Personal Data Controllers, there is an agreement among the Personal  Data Controllers, which defines the role,
responsibilities, and  relationship  between the Personal Data Controllers; interrelated purposes and methods of
processing Personal Data are jointly determined; and
a contact person is jointly appointed.

-A Personal Data Controller and a Personal  Data Processor must appoint an official or officer that protects Personal Data
Data security and confidentiality standa:
-Personal Data shall be processed by protecting the security of Personal Data against unauthorized access, unauthorized disclosure, unlawful alteration, misuse, destruction, and/or removal of the Personal Data
-A Personal Data Controller must protect and ensure the security of Personal Data he/she processes by:

Issuance: Electronic Data Protection Law No.25/NA, 2017
Information asset classification:
Types of Electronic Data:
=General Information: is data of an individual, legal entity or organization that can be accessed, used and disclosed, but the source of the data must be correctly stated.
=Specific/Sensitvie information is information that no individual, legal entity, or organization is allowed to access, use, or disclose without permission from the owner of the information or the relevant organization. Specific information includes government information (official information) and personal information.
Data ownership and accountability rules:
- Data owner: owns electronic data;
 - Data controller: responsible for managing electronic data, such as a ministry, an Internet data center, a telecommunications service provider, an Internet service provider, a bank; it must protect the data under its responsibility so that unauthorized persons cannot access, use, disclose, copy, modify, or delete the data.
Consent management standards:
- The State attaches importance to electronic data protection to ensure the safe use of data and to limit the use or disclosure of data of individuals, legal entities or organizations to the public without permission.
- A person, legal entity or organization that wants to collect data must inform the data owner of the purpose, details of the data to be collected, who will manage it and the rights of the data owner.
Data retention and archiving requirement:
-The data controller may retain electronic data for the period necessary for the purpose of collection and other purposes. Thereafter, personal data may be deleted or access blocked, unless otherwise provided by law.
-The data controller shall delete the electronic data it has collected at the request of the data subject or upon the termination of the purpose of use, the expiry of the collection period
Data sharing and interoperability standa: prohibition on Sending or transferring electronic information without authorization from the owner of the information;
Cross-border data transfer conditions: A person, legal entity or organization may not send or transfer personal data and official data outside the Lao PDR without the consent of the data owner or if it is contrary to the law.
Data quality and integrity standards: Data owners and data managers must check and ensure the accuracy and integrity of data to ensure that the content of electronic data does not conflict with laws and regulations and does not affect socio-economic development, national security, peace and order in society
Encryption/cryptography prescriptions: When sending or transferring important electronic data, such as financial, banking, investment, and accounting data through a computer system, the data controller must encrypt the data and use an electronic certificate approved by the Ministry of Posts, Telecommunications, and Communications to prevent unauthorized persons from accessing, reading, destroying, using, disclosing, sending, transferring, modifying, deleting, altering, and doing other things that cause damage.
Third-party/outsourcing governance: The data controller may not provide personal data it has collected, stored or managed to a third party without the consent of the data owner or with the request of the relevant competent state agency as provided by law.

Issuance: Personal Data Protection Act 2010 (PDPA)
Information asset classification:
The law covers the following:
- personal data:information relating to an identifiable individual in commercial transactions.
-sensitive personal data: data relating to health, religion, political views, criminal offences, or other categories determined by the Minister.
Data ownership and accountability rules: Data user is defined as someone who processes any personal data or has control over or authorizes the processing of any personal data, but does not include a data processor
Data security and confidentiality standa: A data user shall take practical steps to protect personal data from loss, misuse, modification, unauthorized or accidental access or disclosure, alteration, or destruction,Consider the nature/sensitivity of the data and potential harm, the storage location/environment and the security features of the equipment storing the data, and ensure reliability, integrity, and competence of personnel with access and secure transfer of personal data
Data retention and archiving requirement:
(1) The personal data processed for any purpose shall not be kept longer than is necessary for the fulfilment of that purpose.
(2) Data user must take all reasonable steps to ensure that all personal data is destroyed or permanently deleted if it is no longer required for the purpose for which it was to be processed.
Data sharing and interoperability standa:
Data User must not disclose personal data:
- for any purpose other than the purpose for which the data was to be disclosed at the time of collection; or
- to any party not related to that purpose.
Cross-border data transfer conditions:
A Data User may not transfer personal data outside Malaysia unless:

-the destination country is on the Commissioner’s approved list, or
-the data subject has given consent, or
-the transfer is necessary for contractual, legal, or public interest purposes or
-the Data User has taken sufficient safeguards to protect the data.
Data quality and integrity standards:
Data User must take reasonable steps to ensure that the personal data it processes is accurate, complete, not misleading, kept up‑to‑date, having regard to the purpose of the data
Data subjects have the right to access their data and request corrections. This ensures integrity by enabling verification, correction, and updating
Data User to take practical steps to protect the data from loss, misuse, modification, unauthorized access, alteration, or destruction
Incident/breach notification timelines: -Where a data controller has reason to believe that a personal data breach has occurred, the data controller shall, as soon as practicable, notify the Commissioner in the manner and form as determined by the Commissioner
Third-party/outsourcing governance:
Where processing of personal data is carried out by a data
processor on behalf of the data user, the data user shall, for the
purpose of protecting the personal data from any loss, misuse,
modification, unauthorized or accidental access or disclosure,
alteration or destruction, ensure that the data processor—
 (a) provides sufficient guarantees in respect of the technical
and organizational security measures governing the
processing to be carried out; and
 (b) takes reasonable steps to ensure compliance with those
measures

The data controller shall, through a contract or other reasonable means, impose an obligation on the data processor to notify and provide all reasonable and necessary assistance to the data controller in complying with its obligations under Act 709.

Issuance: Circular of the Personal Data Protection Commissioner No. 1/2025 – Data Breach Notification
Data ownership and accountability rules: Data controller's obligation includes notifying the Commissioner and data subjects if the data controller believes that a personal data breach has occurred.
Data security and confidentiality standa: No explicit provision
Consent management standards: No explicit provision
Data retention and archiving requirement: The data controller shall maintain a record of the notification of the personal data breach in physical and electronic form. The record shall be kept for at least two (2) years from the date of the personal data breach.
Incident/breach notification timelines:
Notification to the Commissioner shall be made as soon as practicable in accordance with the procedure provided for
in this Circular.

Data controller must submit to the commissioner within seventy two (72) hours from the occurrence of the personal data breach  the following information:
a) details of the personal data breach that has occurred
b)the likelihood of the personal data breach occuring
c) “the chronology of the incident that resulted in the loss of control over the personal data;”
d) the measures taken or proposed to be taken by the data controller to address the personal data breach, including the measures taken or to be taken to reduce the possible adverse effects of the personal data breach
e) “the measures taken or proposed to be taken to address the affected data subjects;”
f) “the details of the data protection officer or other contact information from whom further information regarding the personal data breach can be obtained.
• If data controller can’t provide the information needed for the notification, such information shall be provided to the Commissioner in stages as soon as practicable and no later than thirty (30) days from the date of the notification made
• Within seven (7) days after the personal data breach notification is made by the data controller to the Commissioner, the data controller shall provide the affected data subjects with the information
Third-party/outsourcing governance: No explicit provision

Personal information refers to any information whether recorded in a material form or not, from which the identity of an individual is apparent or can be reasonably and directly ascertained by the entity holding the information, or when put together with other information would directly and certainly identify an individual.

Sensitive personal information refers to personal information:

(1) About an individual’s race, ethnic origin, marital status, age, color, and religious, philosophical or political affiliations;
(2) About an individual’s health, education, genetic or sexual life of a person, or to any proceeding for any offense committed or alleged to have been committed by such person, the disposal of such proceedings, or the sentence of any court in such proceedings;
(3) Issued by government agencies peculiar to an individual which includes, but not limited to, social security numbers, previous or current health records, licenses or its denials, suspension or revocation, and tax returns; and

Data ownership and accountability rules:
Each personal information controller is responsible for personal information under its control or custody, including information that have been transferred to a third party for processing, whether domestically or internationally, subject to cross-border arrangement and cooperation.

(a) The personal information controller is accountable for complying with the requirements of this Act and shall use contractual or other reasonable means to provide a comparable level of protection while the information are being processed by a third party.

(b) The personal information controller shall designate an individual or individuals who are accountable for the organization’s compliance with this Act. The identity of the individual(s) so designated shall be made known to any data subject upon request.
Data security and confidentiality standa:
SEC. 20. Security of Personal Information. – (a) The personal information controller must implement reasonable and appropriate organizational, physical and technical measures intended for the protection of personal information against any accidental or unlawful destruction, alteration and disclosure, as well as against any other unlawful processing.

(b) The personal information controller shall implement reasonable and appropriate measures to protect personal information against natural dangers such as accidental loss or destruction, and human dangers such as unlawful access, fraudulent misuse, unlawful destruction, alteration and contamination.

(c) The determination of the appropriate level of security under this section must take into account the nature of the personal information to be protected, the risks represented by the processing, the size of the organization and complexity of its operations, current data privacy best practices and the cost of security implementation. Subject to guidelines as the Commission may issue from time to time, the measures implemented must include:

(1) Safeguards to protect its computer network against accidental, unlawful or unauthorized usage or interference with or hindering of their functioning or availability;

(2) A security policy with respect to the processing of personal information;

(3) A process for identifying and accessing reasonably foreseeable vulnerabilities in its computer networks, and for taking preventive, corrective and mitigating action against security incidents that can lead to a security breach; and

(4) Regular monitoring for security breaches and a process for taking preventive, corrective and mitigating action against security incidents that can lead to a security breach.

(d) The personal information controller must further ensure that third parties processing personal information on its behalf shall implement the security measures required by this provision.

(e) The employees, agents or representatives of a personal information controller who are involved in the processing of personal information shall operate and hold personal information under strict confidentiality if the personal information are not intended for public disclosure. This obligation shall continue even after leaving the public service, transfer to another position or upon termination of employment or contractual relations.

(f) The personal information controller shall promptly notify the Commission and affected data subjects when sensitive personal information or other information that may, under the circumstances, be used to enable identity fraud are reasonably believed to have been acquired by an unauthorized person, and the personal information controller or the Commission believes that such unauthorized acquisition is likely to give rise to a real risk of serious harm to any affected data subject. The notification shall at least describe the nature of the breach, the sensitive personal information possibly involved, and the measures taken by the entity to address the breach. Notification may be delayed only to the extent necessary to determine the scope of the breach, to prevent further disclosures, or to restore reasonable integrity to the information and communications system.

(1) In evaluating if notification is unwarranted, the Commission may take into account compliance by the personal information controller with this section and existence of good faith in the acquisition of personal information.

(2) The Commission may exempt a personal information controller from notification where, in its reasonable judgment, such notification would not be in the public interest or in the interests of the affected data subjects.

(3) The Commission may authorize postponement of notification where it may hinder the progress of a criminal investigation related to a serious breach.

Regulator: National Assembly → Government of Viet Nam (central state management authority)
Issuance: Law on Data (No. 60/2024/QH15)
Information asset classification:
Data Classification:
State agencies shall classify data based on requirements for data administration, processing, and protection, including:
a) Classification by the data sharing nature, including common data, private data, and open data;
b) Classification by data importance nature, including core data, important data, and other data;
c) Classification by other criteria, meeting the requirements for data administration, processing, and protection decided by data governing bodies

Further, it distinguishes data through:
Common data: data generally accessed, shared, utilized, and used in agencies of the CPV, the State, the Committee of the Vietnamese Fatherland Front, and socio-political Organizations.
Private data : data accessed, shared, utilized, and used within the internal scope of agencies of the CPV, the State, the Committee of the Vietnamese Fatherland Front, and socio-political organizations.
Important data: data that may affect national defense and security, foreign affairs, macroeconomic situations, social stabilization, and community health and safety, included in the list promulgated by the Prime Minister of Vietnam.
Core data: important data that directly impact national defense and security, foreign affairs, macroeconomic situations, social stabilization, and community health and safety, included in the list promulgated by the Prime Minister of Vietnam.
Data ownership and accountability rules:
'-Data owners refer to agencies, organizations, and individuals with the right to decide on the construction, development, protection, administration, processing, use, and exchange of the value of data under their ownership..
- Data governing bodies shall assess and determine risks and adopt measures to protect data; promptly remedy arising risks and issue notices to data subject matters and relevant agencies, organizations, and individuals.
Data security and confidentiality standa:
'-State agencies shall determine and establish mechanisms for early warnings of risks arising during data processing and develop measures to protect data
-Data governing bodies not prescribed in Clause 2 of this Article shall assess and determine risks and adopt measures to protect data; promptly remedy arising risks and issue notices to data subject matters and relevant agencies, organizations, and individuals.
- Data administration includes the development of policies, plans, programs, processes, and standards concerning data of data owners and data governing bodies in a continuous and effective manner, ensuring the adequacy, accuracy, integrity, consistency, standardization, safety, confidentiality, and timeliness of data.
- Responsibilities of organizations providing products and services concerning data intermediation, data analysis and summary, and data platforms include Manage, inspect, and supervise data safety and confidentiality regularly; prevent, control, and handle data risks; supervise acts that may affect data protection.
Consent management standards: - Private data and data concerning national defense and security, foreign affairs, and cipher shall be stored on the National Data Center's infrastructures upon data owners' consent.
Data retention and archiving requirement:
- Organizations and individuals that are data owners may decide on the storage of data collected, generated, and owned by them; in case of storing core and important data,
- National databases shall be permitted to store data on the infrastructures of the National Data Center.
Data sharing and interoperability standa:
- Data owners and data governing bodies shall conduct data connection and sharing for data users according to the law or under agreements, either in person or through intermediaries
-The Prime Minister of Vietnam shall decide on the sharing of private data under the management of ministries, ministerial agencies, governmental agencies, and provincial People’s Committees in unexpected and urgent cases of preparation and management of natural disasters, epidemics, fire, and explosions or other necessary cases to settle arising issues in reality.
- The disclosure of data shall reflect the correct data from the master data sources, ensuring convenience for organizations and individuals in utilizing, using, and sharing.
- Whether data is subject to disclosure, conditional disclosure, or is not subject to disclosure shall be based on the information reflected by data under the law on information access.
- State agencies shall disclose the list of open data and organize the disclosure of open data according to this Article for utilization, use, and sharing by organizations and individuals. The time of data disclosure for each field shall comply with the law.


'-Other national databases, specialized databases, and information systems of agencies of the CPV, the State, the Vietnamese Fatherland Front, and socio-political organizations shall be connected with the National General Database through data coordination and sharing platforms; national data sharing and integration platforms; provincial and ministerial data sharing and integration platforms, Internet, computer networks, and information systems.
- The data connection and sharing between the National General Database and other databases shall ensure efficiency, safety, and conformity with the functions, tasks, and entitlements of agencies, organizations, and individuals according to the law
- The infrastructures of the National Data Center shall be designed, constructed, and used in compliance with the following requirements: Assurance of the main information technology components of the National Data center, including the National General Database; data coordination and sharing platform"
Data quality and integrity standards:
1. Data quality assurance means assurance of the accuracy, validity, integrity, adequacy, timely update, and consistency of data.
2. State agencies managing databases shall:
a) Synchronously instruct, implement, and apply the national technical regulations and standards concerning data quality assurance and data quality assurance processes for application to databases under their management;
b) Regularly inspect, supervise, and remedy mistakes; synchronize data within their premises and cooperate with relevant agencies and organizations on regular updates, adjustments, and assurance of data quality in the utilization and use.
Third-party/outsourcing governance: No explicit provision

Issuance: Personal Data Protection Law (PDPL) (Law No. 91/2025/QH15, with IRR (Decree 356/2025/ND‑CP )
Information asset classification:
Classification for personal data:
-Basic personal data: personal data that reflects common and identifiable personal elements, frequently used in transactions and social relations,as prescribed in the list issued by the Government.
-Sensitive personal data: personal data associated with the privacy of an individual that, once infringed upon, will directly affect lawful rights and interests of agencies, organizations or individual, as prescribed in the list issued by the Government
Data ownership and accountability rules:
- Personal Data Controller — decides purposes/means of processing
* The personal data controller or the personal data controlling and processing party shall modify personal data upon the request of the data subject or as required by law; and shall request the personal data processor or third party to modify the data subject’s personal data.
-Personal Data Processor — processes data under controller’s instruction
Personal Data Controlling and Processing Party — decides purposes and processes directly
Third Party — involved in personal data processing
Data security and confidentiality standa:
-The deletion or destruction of personal data must be carried out using secure measures to prevent unauthorized access and restoration of the deleted or destroyed personal data.
-During the sensitive personal data processing, the agencies and organizations must establish regulations on access delegation limits, processing procedures, and confidentiality measures.
Data retention and archiving requirement: - Data subjects have the right to request deletion of their personal data.
Data sharing and interoperability standa:
-A method must be established to enable the data subject to refuse data sharing; specify data retention periods; and delete or destroy data when no longer
necessary
- Personal data may only be disclosed for a specific purpose. The scope of disclosure and types of personal data to be disclosed must be consistent with
the intended purpose. The disclosure of personal data must not infringe upon the lawful rights and interests of the data subject.
-Personal data may only be disclosed in the following cases:
*With the consent of the data subject;
* In accordance with the law;
* For the performance of contractual obligations.
Cross-border data transfer conditions:
"1. Cases of cross-border transfer of personal data include:
a) Transfer of personal data stored in Vietnam to a data storage system located outside the territory of the Socialist Republic of Vietnam
b) Agencies, organizations, or individuals in Vietnam transferring personal data to organizations or individuals abroad
c) Vietnam-based or overseas agencies, organizations, or individuals using a platform located outside the territory of the Socialist Republic of Vietnam to
process personal data collected in Vietnam Agencies, organizations, or individuals conducting cross-border
personal data transfer activities must prepare a dossier on the impact assessment of the cross-border transfer of personal data and submit one original copy to the agency in charge of personal data protection within 60 days from the first day of cross-border personal data transfer
-The impact assessment of the cross-border transfer of personal data shall be conducted once for the entire duration of operation of such agency, organization, or individual, and shall be updated
-The agency in charge of personal data protection shall decide to carry out periodic inspections of cross-border personal data transfers not more than once per year, or extraordinary inspections upon detection of violations of the law on personal data protection or when incidents of personal data leakage or loss occur
-The agency in charge of personal data protection shall decide to request the suspension of cross-border personal data transfer by any agency, organization,  or individual upon discovering that the transferred personal data is being used for activities that may harm national defense or national security.
Data quality and integrity standards: Upon receipt of a request to access, correct, or request correction of personal data, or to provide personal data in accordance with proper procedures from a personal data subject, the personal data controller and the personal data controlling and processing party shall respond within 02 working days, provide full information to the personal data subject regarding the procedures, and implement the request within 10 days. In case it is necessary to require a personal data processor or a third party to correct the personal data of a personal data subject, such correction shall be carried out within 15 days.
Encryption/cryptography prescriptions:
-Personal data in big data processing: Implement encryption and anonymization of personal data (the processof separating data that identifies a specific individual for separate storage and security, whereby personal data after such processing is used for processing purposes without being able to identify a specific individual) during the transfer or provision of personal data, except where specialized laws provide otherwise or where processing requires data in clear form for the purposes of crime prevention and control, anti-money laundering, ensuring national security, or handling customer complaints and disputes. In such cases, the agencies and organizations must apply additional security solutions to ensure that personal data is not accessed or used unlawfully

-Personal data protection in blockchain technology: Apply only secure encryption algorithms, hashing algorithms, and digital signature algorithms
-Personal data protection in cloud computing: Personal data stored in cloud computing environments must be encrypted both at rest and during transmission, accompanied by strict access delegation mechanisms
-Personal data processing services: Services for encrypting personal data during transmission and storage
Data Standards (e.g., ISO 20022):
No explicit provision detailing data standards, however required requirements for transfer agreements must include the following content:
- Must specify purpose,
- Types of data,
- Duration,
- Deletion/destruction requirements,
- Responsibilities of parties
